segment.description: Woods Reservoir (AEDC Reservoir), the ~3,600-4,000-acre impoundment at Arnold Air Force Base created by Elk River Dam, Franklin County near Tullahoma/Manchester. Built to supply cooling water for the Arnold Engineering Development Complex wind-tunnel facilities and open to public fishing.
segment.boundaries: Entire reservoir behind Elk River Dam (completed September 1952), fed by Bradley Creek and the upper Elk River drainage; TWRA manages the AEDC Woods Reservoir WMA on its shores.

damTailwater.operator: US Air Force (AEDC Base Civil Engineering, Arnold AFB)
damTailwater.note: Elk River Dam was completed September 1952 expressly to impound a cooling-water supply for AEDC test facilities - i.e., a warm industrial-cooling reservoir, not a cold-release storage project. No documentation of the release draw depth was found; the dam's tailwater is not a trout fishery.

coldSource.notes: Reservoir purpose is cooling-water supply for AEDC per the official Arnold AFB history article; no cold-water habitat design documented anywhere consulted.

holdover.detail: No trout holdover evidence exists for Woods Reservoir: TWRA's Woods Reservoir fishing page documents a warmwater fishery (largemouth/smallmouth/spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish) with no trout program, and the TWRA stocking workbook has zero trout rows for the reservoir. TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 classes hatchery-supported lakes as 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round'.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout presence documented. TWRA lists only warmwater gamefish for the reservoir; the Trout Management Plan places wild trout in East Tennessee mountain waters.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The reservoir exists to supply AEDC cooling water, TWRA documents it solely as a warmwater bass/crappie/catfish fishery, and the TWRA stocking workbook carries zero trout stocking rows for it.
